q-142718:
If the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint distribution with joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & ={f}_{X}(x)={\sum }_{y}f(x,y) \\ P(Y=y) & ={f}_{Y}(y)={\sum }_{x}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

In this case, the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Let's add these row and column totals to our table:

| $f$ | $Y=-1$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.55$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.05$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.45$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.2$ | $0.35$ | $0.45$ | $1$ |

The marginal mass function for $Y$ is given in the following table:

| $y$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.2$ | $0.35$ | $0.45$ |

Finally, using the table of values of the marginal mass function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|Y|>0) & =P(Y\in \{-1,1\}) \\  & =P(Y=-1)+P(Y=1) \\  & =0.2+0.45 \\  & =0.65.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142575:
If the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint distribution with joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & ={f}_{X}(x)={\sum }_{y}f(x,y) \\ P(Y=y) & ={f}_{Y}(y)={\sum }_{x}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

In this case, the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Let's add these row and column totals to our table:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $\frac{3}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{4}{7}$ |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{2}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{3}{7}$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $\frac{5}{7}$ | $\frac{2}{7}$ | $1$ |

The marginal mass function for $Y$ is given in the following table:

| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $\frac{5}{7}$ | $\frac{2}{7}$ |

Finally, using the table of values of the marginal mass function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<2) & =P(Y\in \{1\}) \\  & =P(Y=1) \\  & =\frac{5}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-126740:
The point $P(2,-3,5)$ is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$ At this point, the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve.

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i-3\,j+5\,k \\ 2\sqrt{3-t}\,i+(1-2t)\,j+(t+3)\,k & =2\,i-3\,j+5\,k,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the coefficients of $i,j,$ and $k$ yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3-t}=2 \\ 1-2t=-3 \\ t+3=5\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $t=2.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,-3,5)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(2).$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{3-t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+3)\,k \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3-t}}\,i-2\,j+k \\ {r}^{′}(2) & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3-2}}\,i-2\,j+k \\  & =-\,i-2\,j+k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to the given curve at the point $P(2,-3,5)$ is $-\,i-2\,j+k.$
